content: Repaglinide is prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes, a condition where the body does not use insulin effectively, leading to an inability to regulate blood sugar levels. This medication works by stimulating the pancreas to release insulin, thereby reducing blood glucose levels. It may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Repaglinide is available in tablet form and should be taken orally. The tablets are to be consumed before meals, ideally within 30 minutes prior to eating or immediately before the meal. If you skip a meal, you must also skip the corresponding dose of repaglinide. Conversely, if you add an extra meal, you should take an additional dose. Your doctor may adjust your dosage gradually based on your response to the medication. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take repaglinide exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before starting repaglinide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially those that may interact with repaglinide, such as acetophenazine, aspirin, blood pressure medications, carbamazepine, chloramphenicol, corticosteroids, diuretics, erythromycin, troglitazone, estrogens, isoniazid, ketoconazole, oral contraceptives, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampin, and others. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease or if you have been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking repaglinide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Adhere to all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet, and be aware that alcohol can lower blood sugar levels. Consult your doctor about the safe consumption of alcoholic beverages while on this medication. If you miss a dose of repaglinide and have just started eating a meal, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if you have already finished eating, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Repaglinide may cause fluctuations in blood sugar levels. Be familiar with the symptoms of both low (hypoglycemia) and high (hyperglycemia) blood sugar, and know how to respond if these symptoms occur. Hypoglycemia symptoms include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, irritability, mood changes, headache, numbness or tingling around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, and clumsy or jerky movements. Severe hypoglycemia can lead to confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness, requiring immediate medical attention. Ensure that family, friends, and those around you are aware of these symptoms and know how to assist you in an emergency. Hyperglycemia symptoms include extreme thirst, frequent urination, excessive hunger, weakness, and blurred vision. Untreated hyperglycemia can result in diabetic ketoacidosis, a life-threatening condition. Symptoms of ketoacidosis include dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, and decreased consciousness. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Common side effects of repaglinide include headache, nasal congestion, joint pain, back pain, constipation, and diarrhea. Notify your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Store repaglinide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular monitoring of your blood sugar and HbA1c levels to assess your response to the medication. Your doctor will also instruct you on how to monitor your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Always wear a diabetic identification bracelet to ensure proper treatment in emergencies. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
